newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude recovers after EIA data released.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude recovers after EIA data released.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures recovered after bouncing off support and into positive territory, helped by U.S. EIA statistical data which confirmed a fall in crude and distillates stocks.
December Brent took heart from a stronger NYMEX open to trade six cents up at $24.00 a barrel at 1346 GMT.

"The rally we've had so far has been as much on short-covering pulling us back to unchanged until the New York open. The EIAs will not have had a negative effect on the market," said Alistair Harris of Mees Pierson brokerage.
"It's moving in very light volume. We had a dip down, we found support at $23.70 on Brent and we are looking for $225 support on gas oil," he added.
Brent fell 21 cents during the morning session to an intra-day low of $23.72 a barrel and November gas oil was down to $222 a tonne, down $5.50. It was trading 50 cents up at $228 at 1351 GMT.
Dealers said markets opened steadier after a late rally on Wednesday wiped out some of the much steeper losses, which at one point had traders worried about a wholesale selloff.
Failure to break resistance at new five-year highs and talk that the U.S. Energy Department might intervene on heating oil exports to Europe was behind a heating oil slump.

Oil company executives and a Justice Department representative will meet Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary on Friday to discuss what can be done to ensure low heating oil stocks do not hit consumers too hard this winter.
The Energy Information Administration (EIA) data showed U.S. crude stocks were 3.3 million barrels down in the week ending October 11 while distillate stocks were off 900,000 barrels.
